item.title: Ransomware Affiliates Weigh AI Pentesting Tools Against Operational Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 19:00 → 22 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Top Ransomware Gangs & AI Pentesting Tools — Optional

Top ransomware affiliates have not broadly adopted autonomous AI pentesting frameworks because their proven access-broker model and manual Windows/ESXi tradecraft are stealthier, more reliable, and more cost-effective. AI is more likely being used quietly for operator assistance, while smaller crews absorb the expense and OPSEC risks of agentic tooling.

  • The article says established ransomware affiliates such as Akira, Qilin, and Rhysida have not been widely reported using autonomous AI offensive frameworks such as ARTEX, Cairn, or PentAGI.
  • Smaller or newer extortion groups, including WhiteArmor, Settra, and n0n, have been observed experimenting with AI tools, sometimes with poor operational security.
  • Top ransomware affiliates often purchase pre-vetted corporate access from initial access brokers and focus on internal actions such as moving through Windows domains, stealing data, and targeting VMware ESXi systems.
  • The article argues that cloud-based AI services can create logging, account-suspension, attribution, and cost risks, while locally hosting capable models requires expensive hardware and operational effort.
  • SOCRadar reported cases involving INC/Lynx and TheGentlemen affiliates using AI-based frameworks, with reported OpenRouter costs of $4,500 and $23,900 respectively.

Technologies: firewall, hypervisor, iam, orchestration

Products: artex, cairn, cyberstrikeai, pentagi, phantom, fortigate, vmware-esxi, claude-opus, opencode, active-directory

Vendors: fortinet, vmware, openrouter, anthropic, microsoft

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Compromise, Cleverbridge Card Theft, and Signal AI Privacy Controls
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 15:00 → 22 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices — Should Read

Attackers exploited a flaw in GL.iNet’s GoodCloud remote-management service to install persistent malware and reverse shells on routers and KVM devices, potentially exposing connected systems. GL.iNet has blocked the attack path and urges customers to update firmware, scan devices, preserve evidence, reset compromised systems, and rotate credentials.

  • GL.iNet confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote-management services to access customer routers and KVM devices and install malicious software.
  • GL.iNet says it blocked the attack path and fixed the cloud vulnerability, but those measures do not remove malware from devices already infected.
  • Researchers and users reported persistent backdoors and root-level reverse shells on affected devices, including outbound connections to 170.39.226[.]219.
  • A malicious ni.sh script tailored for GL.iNet devices downloads payloads, creates persistence through startup scripts and scheduled tasks, and can hide connections by replacing the legitimate netstat utility.
  • GL.iNet recommends installing the latest security firmware, using its linked detection and cleanup tool, preserving evidence before resets, avoiding restoration of old configurations, and rotating exposed credentials or access keys.

Technologies: cloud-platform, router, remote-access, iot-device

Products: goodcloud, astrowarp, gl-rm1, gl-mt2500, rm10, rmq1

Vendors: gl-inet, remote-tohome-consulting

Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach — Should Read

E-commerce platform Cleverbridge says attackers stole customers’ payment card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV/CVC codes after unauthorized activity was detected on November 4, 2026. The company is notifying affected customers, offering credit monitoring, and advises them to watch for fraudulent charges and contact their card issuers.

  • Cleverbridge detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026, temporarily took systems offline, and later determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on its platform.
  • A breach notification shared with BleepingComputer states that the stolen information included payment card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV/CVC security codes.
  • Cleverbridge says no other personal data, such as names, contact information, or billing details, were copied.
  • The company began notifying affected customers on November 20 and is working with TransUnion’s Cyberscout to provide credit monitoring and fraud assistance.
  • Cleverbridge said the incident was not ransomware and that its systems were not encrypted by the attackers.

Products: cyberscout

Vendors: cleverbridge, transunion

Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android — Should Read

Signal is adding protections on iOS and Android to prevent Siri and Gemini AI assistants from reading or capturing private chats, extending similar defenses previously introduced for Microsoft Recall. The safeguards are automatic where supported, though iOS screenshot blocking may also prevent users from taking their own Signal screenshots.

  • Signal announced protections intended to block Siri on iOS 27 and AI assistants such as Gemini from capturing Signal conversations on supported Android devices.
  • Signal said the measures are designed to prevent operating-system AI features, including Siri’s Onscreen Awareness and Google’s Gemini Intelligence, from accessing chat content displayed on screen.
  • On iOS, users can check Settings > App Security to confirm that Block Siri AI is enabled, while Android enables Screen Security automatically when Signal detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen.
  • Signal warned that the iOS protection also blocks users from taking screenshots of their own Signal conversations.
  • Signal said it currently cannot provide screenshot-blocking protection on macOS and recommends macOS 27 users add Signal to the Excluded Apps list in System Settings > Siri.

Technologies: mobile-os, operating-system

Products: signal, siri, gemini, microsoft-recall, ios-27, android, macos-27, windows-11

Vendors: signal, apple, google, microsoft

item.title: OpenRouter Prompt Theft and Ghostscript CVE-2026-125396 Sandbox Escape
item.content:encoded:
Window: 22 Nov 03:00 → 22 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms — Should Read

Dragos found that attackers and unscrupulous AI inference providers had been copying customer prompts, including Zero Data Retention requests, for months, exposing credentials and sensitive data. OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility while notifying potentially affected users.

  • Dragos seeded roughly two million AI prompts with unique links and credentials between July and November and found evidence that data from three AI inference providers had been copied for months.
  • Some copied requests were marked Zero Data Retention, a setting intended to ensure that prompts are not stored.
  • OpenRouter said it removed three providers from its platform, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, and notified potentially affected customers.
  • Researchers observed attackers using stolen planted AWS keys to list S3 buckets, search AWS Secrets Manager and Parameter Store, and attempt to create Bedrock API keys and IAM users.
  • Phala, Together AI, and Novita each publicly disclosed separate incidents involving exposure, storage, or unintended forwarding of customer AI requests.

Technologies: api-gateway, cloud-platform, object-storage, secrets-manager

Products: openrouter, artex, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, minimax-m3, glm-5-2, kimi-k2-6, amazon-s3, aws-secrets-manager, amazon-bedrock, feishu

Vendors: openrouter, dragos, phala, together-ai, novita, minimax, deepseek, amazon-web-services, feishu

Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps — Should Read

A patched Ghostscript use-after-free flaw (CVE-2026-125396) lets crafted uploaded documents bypass the -dSAFER sandbox and execute commands on servers through common rendering paths in apps such as WordPress, Roundcube, and ImageMagick. Organizations should update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or later, including copies embedded in containers and application bundles.

  • Ghostscript flaw CVE-2026-125396 allowed crafted files to bypass its -dSAFER protections and run commands on the server processing them.
  • The issue was a use-after-free bug in Ghostscript's font-loading code, and Artifex fixed it in Ghostscript version 10.08.0 on September 8.
  • pwn.ai demonstrated that upload, preview, and print features in about ten applications could route crafted PostScript or EPS content to Ghostscript, including through image and document libraries.
  • Some tested paths required no login, including anonymous jobs sent to a shared Debian 13 print queue, Roundcube email attachments processed when opened, and public WordPress plugin upload forms.
  • Updating only the host operating system may not fix the exposure if an application or container includes its own older Ghostscript copy.

Technologies: cms, operating-system

Products: ghostscript, wordpress-core, imagemagick, pillow, libvips, roundcube, forminator, essential-addons-for-elementor, debian-linux, suse-linux-enterprise, opensuse-leap, apparmor

Vendors: artifex, wordpress, google, imagemagick, roundcube, suse, debian

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposed Customer Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 19:00 → 21 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets — Should Read

Rackspace Spot was breached using leaked credentials, allowing attackers to impersonate users, deploy unauthorized Kubernetes pods, and access secrets that may contain passwords, API keys, and tokens. Affected customers should rotate exposed credentials and review logs from November 17 for misuse.

  • Rackspace said an unauthorized party used leaked credentials to access parts of its Rackspace Spot cloud platform on November 17, 2026.
  • The attackers could act as legitimate users in some customer organizations, create Kubernetes pods, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes.
  • Rackspace warned that any Secret in an affected user’s clusters, along with that user’s Spot API and refresh tokens, could have been exposed.
  • Rackspace revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed unauthorized pods, rotated keys, and restored the Spot service on November 21 after temporarily disabling access.
  • Affected customers were told to reissue tokens, replace automation refresh tokens, obtain new Kubernetes configuration files, rotate stored credentials, and examine relevant logs dating from November 17.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, secrets-manager

Products: rackspace-spot, kubernetes

Vendors: rackspace, platform9, kubernetes

item.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health Data Exposure and BADBOX 3.0 Ad Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 15:00 → 21 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data — Should Read

Microsoft fixed an Entra Connect Health API flaw that attackers exploited to access tenant contact and configuration metadata, including administrator email addresses, but not passwords, tokens, or active cryptographic keys. Affected organizations should watch for targeted phishing, enforce phishing-resistant MFA for privileged accounts, and review Entra logs and Connect Health settings.

  • Microsoft said attackers exploited a vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API to obtain unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level contact and configuration metadata.
  • The exposed data included technical contact and administrator email addresses, tenant IDs and names, initial domain names, country and regional information, Entra license tiers, directory synchronization status, and Connect Health onboarding status.
  • Microsoft said passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, on-premises Active Directory topology details, and Azure subscription information were not exposed.
  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19, 2026, completed its investigation on November 20, and began notifying affected organizations.
  • Microsoft advised organizations to prepare for targeted phishing or social-engineering attempts, use phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for privileged accounts, and review Connect Health configurations and Entra audit and sign-in logs.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, network-monitoring

Products: microsoft-entra-connect-health, microsoft-entra-admin-center, microsoft-entra, azure-service-health

Vendors: microsoft

BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests — Should Read

BADBOX 3.0 rebuilt after prior disruptions and became the largest documented ad-fraud botnet, generating up to 40 billion fraudulent daily ad bid requests through compromised low-cost Android devices. It also covertly enrolls infected devices in residential proxy networks, and researchers warn its operators are likely to adapt again after the latest takedowns.

  • HUMAN reported that BADBOX 3.0 generated roughly 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day at its peak, representing more than 4% of connected-TV traffic observed by its platform.
  • BADBOX 3.0 infects low-cost Android Open Source Project phones, tablets, and streaming TV boxes to run hidden video ads while impersonating legitimate streaming applications.
  • The botnet also enrolled infected devices into 11 residential proxy networks without owners' knowledge, including PXYEDGE, which HUMAN identified as a rebranded successor to IpMoYu.
  • HUMAN linked the operation to a Chinese electronics manufacturer through associated domains, device-specific code checks, a factory-installed TV launcher, and a repository maintainer.
  • HUMAN, Google, and other partners disrupted BADBOX 3.0 infrastructure, but HUMAN warned that the operators are likely to adapt to the latest disruption.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, proxy

Products: android, android-tv, t95-android-tv-box, pxyedge, ipmoyu

Vendors: google, human-security, android-open-source-project

item.title: Critical GPGME and MONAI Label Flaws Highlight AI-Assisted Exploitation Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 11:00 → 21 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys — Should Read

GnuPG has patched a critical double-free flaw (CVE-2026-129975) in GPGME that malicious OpenPGP keys could use to expose application data and potentially enable remote code execution. Users should update to GPGME 2.3.1, Gpg4win 5.1.2, or rebuild applications with bundled or statically linked vulnerable copies.

  • GnuPG warned that CVE-2026-129975 is a critical double-free flaw in GPGME triggered by malicious OpenPGP keys with unusually long user IDs.
  • The flaw affects software using GPGME versions before 2.3.0, including shared, Windows DLL, and statically linked installations.
  • Affected software can include many mail and XMPP clients, Samba, Gpg4win, GnuPG Desktop, and GnuPG VS-Desktop.
  • GnuPG has released GPGME 2.3.1 and Gpg4win 5.1.2 to address the issue, while the legacy branch received version 1.24.4.
  • The project reported no known exploitation, but said the flaw could expose application data and that remote code execution cannot be ruled out.

Products: gpgme, gpg4win, gnupg-desktop, gnupg-vs-desktop, samba

Vendors: gnupg-project, gitlab

Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access — Should Read

China-linked operators reportedly used Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical path-traversal zero-day in exposed MONAI Label servers, achieving root access on at least one university system. No patched release is available yet, so organizations should restrict network exposure, enable authentication, and run MONAI Label with minimal privileges.

  • Suspected China-linked operators used Cairn, an open-source AI-agent framework, to discover and exploit a previously unknown path-traversal flaw in MONAI Label.
  • The flaw affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier default installations, where authentication is disabled and user-provided file identifiers can cause files to be written outside the intended storage folder.
  • Amazon Threat Intelligence reported that the agents reached the ability to write files to a university server in roughly 11 minutes and later obtained root access on one server by placing a Python startup file and triggering a training feature.
  • Project MONAI merged a source-code fix on October 19, but its advisory says no patched release is yet available; the CVE record identifies the issue as CVE-2026-133968 with a critical 9.8 score.
  • Organizations running MONAI Label should restrict untrusted network access, enable authentication, use limited service accounts, confirm source builds include the fix, and inspect exposed systems for unexpected Python startup files or unusual training jobs.

Products: monai-label, cairn

Vendors: amazon, project-monai

A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats — Should Read

Researchers showed that a malicious webpage could hijack Meta Muse’s cloud environment to access and alter private chats, memories, and potentially connected-account credentials, though the attack was contained to one user’s machine. NebuSec said Meta fixed the reported flaws before disclosure.

  • NebuSec researchers demonstrated that a malicious webpage could extract and alter Meta Muse users’ private conversations and stored memories without showing an approval prompt.
  • The researchers chained a flaw in Muse’s built-in browser with a Linux kernel flaw to take full control of an individual user’s cloud machine.
  • Full control of the cloud machine could reach Muse’s credential store, saved files, and Sentinel monitoring layer, although the test did not escape to the underlying shared server or other users’ machines.
  • The demonstration was conducted in a laboratory and did not target real users, according to the article.
  • NebuSec said it reported the findings to Meta Muse’s team and that all described exploits were fixed before publication.

Technologies: cloud-platform, operating-system

Products: meta-muse, sentinel, linux-kernel

Vendors: meta, nebusec, linux-kernel-project

item.title: Signal Blocks AI Chat Screenshots as CISA Flags Exploited VMware, Cisco, Apache Flaws
item.content:encoded:
Window: 21 Nov 07:00 → 21 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge — Must Read

CISA added four actively exploited flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, urging U.S. federal agencies to patch by November 23, 2026. The VMware vCenter flaw has been linked to suspected China-nexus espionage group Armory Castle, while Cisco Expressway was used in a breach of a Russian organization.

  • CISA added four vulnerabilities affecting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after finding evidence of active exploitation.
  • The Apache Roller flaw, CVE-2026-129448, can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code through its XML-RPC endpoint, and Apache Roller maintainers said it is being actively exploited.
  • CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to run commands as root on a clustered device through the database service.
  • A suspected China-nexus espionage group called Armory Castle reportedly used the VMware vCenter authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-123890 alongside a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw to install custom backdoors and steal data.
  • U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies were directed to patch all four vulnerabilities by November 23, 2026.

Technologies: cms, hypervisor, remote-access, web-server

Products: apache-roller, cisco-expressway, sap-netweaver-enterprise-portal, vmware-vcenter, beyondtrust-remote-support

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, cisco, sap, broadcom, vmware, beyondtrust

Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS — Should Read

Signal now blocks screenshots by default on supported Android and iOS devices to limit OS-level AI agents from reading private chats, though it acknowledges the safeguard cannot prevent all data-access paths. The change follows concerns that agents with broad accessibility, screenshot, or notification permissions can extract Signal content outside the app’s encryption protections.

  • Signal will restrict screenshots by default on supported Android and iOS devices to prevent operating-system AI agents from reading private chats, while acknowledging that the protection is incomplete.
  • Signal says users can disable the setting through its privacy and app-security controls, but doing so may expose their Signal content and their contacts’ content to AI agents.
  • Signal warned that screenshot blocking cannot prevent AI agents from obtaining data through other routes, including files already on a user’s device.
  • Reuters reported that Meta’s Muse AI agent accessed Signal messages on Apple and Android devices by using broad permissions, including macOS accessibility and screenshot tools and Android push-notification access.
  • Signal is urging technology companies to provide documented app-level controls that can fully opt apps out of AI data access and processing.

Technologies: mobile-os, operating-system

Products: signal, muse, siri, gemini, windows-recall, ios-27, android, windows-11, macos

Vendors: signal-foundation, meta, apple, google, microsoft

The Asana Digest Said Tuesday. It Arrived on a Thursday. — May Read

A phishing email reused a genuine Asana digest template and assets but was sent through an unrelated Uruguayan domain via Amazon SES, with one malicious Lovable-hosted link substituted for a legitimate button. The mismatched weekday and date exposed the recycled template, underscoring that authentic branding and passing email authentication do not prove a message came from the claimed service.

  • A regional airport authority’s accounts-receivable mailbox received an email that copied an Asana daily task digest but was sent from an unrelated .com.uy domain through Amazon SES.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks for the sending domain, but none of those checks showed that Asana sent it.
  • The email’s heading said Tuesday next to October 1, 2026, a Thursday, while an embedded Asana tracking pixel indicated that the original template had been generated on Tuesday, August 18, 2026.
  • The attacker changed the subject line and replaced the main “View in Ticket” button with a link to a malicious Lovable-hosted page, while retaining the other genuine Asana links and branding.
  • The incident was automatically classified as phishing and the message was removed from the mailbox.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: asana, amazon-ses, lovable, outlook-on-the-web, adaptive-ai

Vendors: asana, amazon-web-services, lovable, microsoft, ironscales

item.title: Ruby2Shell and phpAfterShell RCE Flaws Drive Urgent Patching and WAF Defenses
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Nov 19:00 → 20 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

phpAfterShell: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-115560 & CVE-2026-126714) — Must Read

PHP patched two critical session-handling flaws, CVE-2026-115560 and CVE-2026-126714, that could enable unauthenticated remote code execution on affected servers. Upgrade to PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, or later immediately, and temporarily disable session upload progress if patching is delayed.

  • PHP released security updates on November 19, 2026, addressing 17 advisories covering 18 CVE identifiers, including seven critical-severity issues.
  • CVE-2026-115560 is a session serialization mismatch involving PHP session upload progress that can lead to object deserialization and remote code execution.
  • CVE-2026-126714 affects PHP's built-in files session handler, where interrupted writes can leave mixed session data that may later be interpreted as serialized objects.
  • Both vulnerabilities affect PHP 8.2.0 through 8.2.35, 8.3.0 through 8.3.36, 8.4.0 through 8.4.27, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.12.
  • PHP fixed both issues in versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, and 8.5.13, and the article states that no public exploit code or active exploitation had been identified at the time of writing.

Technologies: web-server

Products: php, ext-session, php-fpm, netspi-easm, netspi-ptaas

Vendors: php, netspi, synack

How Cloudflare WAF protects against ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825) — Must Read

Cloudflare has added default-blocking WAF rules for ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825), a critical Ruby string case-conversion flaw that can enable pre-authentication RCE in default Rails and Sinatra deployments. The WAF is only a temporary safeguard: organizations should immediately upgrade to Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, or 4.0.10 and update affected bundled products.

  • Ruby disclosed ruby2shell (CVE-2026-132825), a critical heap buffer overflow in string case conversion that Ruby says can lead to remote code execution in some scenarios.
  • The flaw affects Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, Ruby 3.4.0 through 3.4.12, and Ruby 4.0.0 through 4.0.9; fixes are available in Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, and 4.0.10.
  • Default Ruby on Rails and classic-style Sinatra applications can reach the vulnerable code before authentication through a crafted multipart POST request using the _method parameter.
  • Cloudflare added default-blocking managed WAF rules for ruby2shell and the related Ruby integer-overflow issue GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px for Free and paid customers.
  • Cloudflare states that WAF protection is a compensating control rather than a replacement for patching, because traffic that bypasses Cloudflare and non-HTTP inputs can still reach vulnerable Ruby code.

Technologies: waf

Products: cloudflare-waf, ruby, ruby-on-rails, sinatra, rack, gitlab, github-enterprise-server, mastodon, openproject, discourse, chatwoot

Vendors: cloudflare, ruby, gitlab, github, mastodon, openproject, discourse, chatwoot

Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists — Should Read

Com-affiliated extortion groups, including Bling Libra and newly tracked clusters Vortex and Cinder, are using IT-support vishing and adversary-in-the-middle phishing to steal cloud credentials, enroll rogue MFA devices and exfiltrate Microsoft 365 data. Organizations should harden help-desk identity verification, deploy phishing-resistant MFA, restrict browser extensions and monitor identity changes and bulk cloud-data exports.

  • Unit 42 reported sustained vishing-led data theft and extortion activity by Com-affiliated actors, including Bling Libra, against financial services, healthcare and legal organizations primarily in the United States, United Kingdom and Australia.
  • The newly tracked CL-CRI-1264 (Vortex) cluster primarily targeted healthcare, pharmaceutical and medical organizations, used fake IT-support calls and organization-specific phishing sites, and enrolled unauthorized MFA devices after capturing credentials.
  • CL-CRI-1274 (Cinder) replayed persistent sign-in session tokens, used Python and the Microsoft Graph SDK to collect data from SharePoint and OneDrive, and sent internal email and Microsoft Teams extortion messages.
  • Unit 42 identified a malicious sideloaded browser extension masquerading as Google Chrome that can record keystrokes, steal authentication cookies and browser data, capture webcam feeds, and remotely control Chromium-based browsers.
  • The article recommends tightening help-desk verification, adopting phishing-resistant MFA such as FIDO2 or passkeys, allowing only approved browser extensions, monitoring identity-related actions, and alerting on unauthorized data exports.

Technologies: browser, cloud-platform, identity-provider, iam, mfa, proxy

Products: microsoft-365, microsoft-teams, sharepoint, onedrive, microsoft-graph, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, duo, cloudflare-pages, doko-panel

Vendors: palo-alto-networks, microsoft, google, cloudflare, okta, cisco

JPMorganChase, Mastercard and Visa Third-Party Security Breaches and What SaaS Posture and Detection Can Surface — Should Read

JPMorganChase, Visa, and Mastercard reported third-party breaches exposing limited marketing or contact data, while an unconfirmed link to Qubole coincides with research showing stolen vendor credentials can abuse dormant trusted cloud access. Organizations should inventory, restrict, monitor, and rapidly revoke third-party SaaS integrations, OAuth grants, and service accounts.

  • JPMorganChase, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed third-party incidents on November 19, 2026, and said payment data and their core systems were not affected.
  • JPMorganChase said marketing data held by vendors may include customer names and email addresses, while Mastercard said a limited number of email addresses from one cardholder benefit program were exposed.
  • The extortion group n0n claimed it breached Qubole and posted files it said came from suppliers serving the three companies, but neither the Qubole connection nor the leaked data has been verified.
  • Wiz, Sentra, and Mandiant separately documented attackers using credentials associated with Qubole to access customer cloud environments through trusted roles, including roles that were largely dormant.
  • The article recommends inventorying and limiting third-party application access, monitoring unusual integration behavior, and being able to quickly disable integrations and rotate their credentials.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, secrets-manager, iam

Products: qubole, amazon-s3, aws-lambda, aws-secrets-manager, aws-systems-manager-parameter-store, microsoft-entra-id, okta, salesforce, microsoft-365, servicenow

Vendors: qubole, amazon-web-services, wiz, sentra, mandiant, appomni, salesforce, microsoft, okta, servicenow

US companies’ use of Chinese open weight AI draws rebuke from House chairmen — Should Read

A bipartisan House report warns that U.S. companies adopting China-developed open-weight AI models could create long-term national-security and supply-chain risks, comparing the potential dependence to past concerns over Huawei and ZTE. It urges U.S. investment in open-weight AI and restrictions on Chinese models in federal and critical-infrastructure use.

  • A joint House Homeland Security Committee and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party report warns that U.S. companies are embedding China-developed open-weight AI models into their technology systems.
  • The report cites Airbnb, DoorDash, and Cursor owner Anysphere as companies using Chinese open-weight models for customer assistance, coding projects, and inventory work.
  • The lawmakers warn that widespread adoption of these models could make them difficult and costly to remove later, drawing a comparison to concerns about Huawei and ZTE technology.
  • The report says Chinese open-weight models are being adopted because they are inexpensive, easily customized, and effective, while citing federal findings that Chinese developers used proxy networks and fraudulent accounts to obtain outputs from U.S. frontier models.
  • Its 12 recommendations include creating an American open-weight AI initiative, requiring standards for model sourcing and AI component records, barring China-developed models from federal contracts and sensitive critical-infrastructure roles, and systematically evaluating Chinese models.

Products: cursor

Vendors: anysphere

Container Store restores systems after cyberattack — Should Read

The Container Store restored its website and internal systems after a cyberattack that disrupted online orders and in-store payments, though stores remained open using alternative processing. The n0n extortion group has claimed the retailer, but the company says there is currently no evidence that customer financial data was stolen.

  • The Container Store restored its website and systems after a cyberattack disrupted online ordering and limited in-store transaction processing.
  • The retailer’s stores remained open during the disruption but used alternative procedures to process transactions.
  • Neighborhood Intelligence said the incident affected only The Container Store and did not affect Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY, or Kirkland’s.
  • The company said it hired cybersecurity experts to contain the incident and restore affected systems, and it currently does not appear that customer financial data was stolen.
  • The n0n cybercriminal group listed The Container Store on its leak site, but the company did not address the group’s claims.

Health-ISAC Hacking Healthcare 11-19-2026 — May Read

The United States and European Union have launched new healthcare cybersecurity initiatives focused on improving hospital resilience, risk assessment, monitoring, incident response, and continuity of care. The U.S. Project Lifeline 250 targets rural hospitals in South Carolina through public-private support, while the EU is funding seven projects aligned with its healthcare cybersecurity action plan and NIS2 compliance.

  • The White House Office of the National Cyber Director and South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster announced Project Lifeline 250 on October 26 as a six-month pilot to strengthen cybersecurity at rural hospitals.
  • Project Lifeline 250 will connect rural hospitals with government and private-sector participants that provide tools and services to identify weaknesses, improve cybersecurity, and reduce disruptions from cyber incidents.
  • Microsoft, Trellix, Zscaler, and Cisco are participating in Project Lifeline 250.
  • The European Commission and European Cybersecurity Competence Centre announced seven Digital Europe Programme-funded healthcare cybersecurity projects on November 6.
  • The seven EU projects cover risk and maturity assessments, staff training and awareness, AI-driven cybersecurity tools, continuity of care, recovery, and support for NIS2 compliance.

Vendors: microsoft, trellix, zscaler, cisco

West Virginia Legislature hit with cyber incident affecting IT systems — May Read

A cyber incident has disrupted the West Virginia Legislature’s website and certain IT systems, prompting containment measures and an outside investigation. Officials say the impact appears limited to legislative systems, with no other state agencies affected so far.

  • A cyber incident that began Thursday disrupted the West Virginia Legislature’s website and affected its IT systems through Friday.
  • The Legislature temporarily disabled access to certain IT systems while it contained the incident and investigated with outside cybersecurity specialists.
  • Officials said the incident appears limited to the Legislature’s computer systems and that no other West Virginia state agencies or offices are affected.
  • The Legislature had not said whether the incident involved ransomware, and no hacking group had claimed responsibility as of Friday.
  • Comparitech recorded 132 ransomware attacks against U.S. government bodies in the third quarter, a 91% increase over the same quarter last year.

Vendors: recorded-future, comparitech

What’s New in Netskope’s FedRAMP High Environment — Optional

Netskope has expanded its FedRAMP High-authorized NewEdge Government platform with Enterprise Browser, Skylight AI Gateway, DLP on Demand, and additional Digital Experience Management capabilities for U.S. federal agencies.

  • Netskope has added Enterprise Browser, Skylight AI Gateway, DLP on Demand, and expanded Digital Experience Management capabilities to its FedRAMP High-authorized NewEdge Government offering.
  • Netskope One Enterprise Browser is generally available in FedRAMP High environments and lets agencies apply data-protection and activity controls to browser sessions on Windows and macOS.
  • Netskope Skylight AI Gateway provides real-time visibility, inline policy enforcement, and data protection for interactions between agency applications, APIs, and privately hosted or public AI services.
  • The customer-hosted Netskope One DLP on Demand virtual appliance now supports FedRAMP High, extending data inspection into customer-managed on-premises and cloud environments.
  • DEM Professional, Enterprise Starter, and Enterprise are now available in FedRAMP High to help agencies monitor user experience, network connectivity, and application performance.

Technologies: browser, dlp, api-gateway, network-monitoring

Products: netskope-newedge-government, netskope-one, netskope-one-enterprise-browser, netskope-skylight-ai-gateway, netskope-one-dlp-on-demand, netskope-one-dem

Vendors: netskope

Score It, Prove It, Clear It: Medical Device Security in the Enforcement Era — Optional

Medcrypt’s recorded webinar explains that FDA medical-device cybersecurity reviews increasingly hinge on concrete implementation evidence, not just security program design. It covers CVSS exploitability, risk registers, and pre-filing checks intended to reduce submission refusals.

  • Health-ISAC published a recording of a Medcrypt webinar featuring Seth Carmody and Axel Wirth on FDA cybersecurity enforcement for medical devices.
  • The webinar states that nearly half of FDA deficiencies are now cybersecurity-related.
  • The webinar highlights that implementation evidence, rather than program design alone, distinguishes cleared device submissions from refused ones.
  • The session discusses using CVSS exploitability without treating the total CVSS score as risk.
  • The webinar presents five pre-filing checks tied to real refusal grounds and describes using a universal risk register to connect vulnerability scores with patient-harm decisions expected by the FDA.

Vendors: medcrypt

item.title: Cairn AI Zero-Day Exploitation, Bell Canada Breach, and Android Malware
item.content:encoded:
Window: 20 Nov 15:00 → 20 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university — Should Read

Amazon says suspected Chinese hackers used the autonomous Cairn AI penetration-testing framework to identify and exploit an apparent zero-day path traversal flaw in MONAI Label, compromising two East Asian universities. The case highlights how AI agents can autonomously conduct prolonged, high-speed intrusion attempts and discover previously unknown vulnerabilities.

  • Amazon Threat Intelligence said suspected Chinese operators used the open-source Cairn autonomous AI penetration-testing framework while targeting universities in East Asia.
  • According to Amazon, Cairn agents found and exploited an unpatched path traversal flaw in the open-source MONAI Label medical imaging AI application, which Amazon assessed with high confidence was a zero-day.
  • The operators used the same apparent zero-day to breach a second university, and Project MONAI later fixed the flaw after Amazon contacted its maintainers.
  • Amazon said one unsuccessful Cairn attempt performed 148 actions over 16 hours, while another tested more than 30,000 credential combinations associated with 80 real usernames over more than six hours.
  • The article notes that Artex, Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, and PentAGI are among autonomous multi-agent offensive frameworks highlighted in recent reporting and research.

Products: cairn, monai-label, artex

Vendors: amazon, project-monai

Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info — Should Read

JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard reported that a cyberattack on a third-party provider exposed limited customer marketing data, mainly names and email addresses, while payment systems and card data were not affected. The n0n ransomware group claims the provider was Qubole and says it leaked stolen data after accessing customer AWS environments with compromised credentials.

  • JPMorgan Chase said a cyberattack targeting third-party service providers may have exposed customer names and email addresses contained in vendor-held marketing data.
  • Visa said its systems were not involved in the third-party incident and that no payment data, including card numbers, was affected.
  • Mastercard said a third-party provider exposed a limited number of email addresses belonging to a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program.
  • The n0n ransomware group claimed responsibility for an attack on Qubole and alleged it used compromised Qubole credentials to access customer AWS environments between October 14 and 26, 2026.
  • n0n claimed it leaked Chase, Visa, and Mastercard data on its extortion site on November 16, 2026.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: qubole, aws-iam

Vendors: qubole, idera, amazon-web-services

Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data — Should Read

Bell Canada says an unidentified “agentic” threat actor breached multiple systems on November 17, 2026, including a pre-production Maximo environment used to order and provision telecom circuits. Enterprise customer business contact details, ticket titles, and some network-related IP information may have been stolen, though Bell says no credentials or highly sensitive personal data were exposed.

  • Bell Canada confirmed that an unidentified “agentic” threat actor accessed some of its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data.
  • The intruder accessed a pre-production environment of Bell’s Maximo system, which is used to order and provision telecommunications network connections.
  • Potentially exposed information includes business names, job titles, corporate email addresses, phone numbers, business addresses, ticket titles, and some IP addresses associated with network elements or systems.
  • Bell said the affected data did not include credentials, highly sensitive personal information, PDFs, file attachments, or other supplementary information stored in Maximo.
  • Bell said it contained the incident, customer services were not affected, and it is sharing indicators and threat-hunting information with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

Products: maximo

Vendors: bell-canada, ibm

Bazuka Android Malware Uses Fake Screen Overlays to Hide Credential Theft and Device Control — Should Read

Researchers uncovered Bazuka, a modular Android banking-malware framework that uses deceptive screen overlays, keylogging, NFC and SMS/2FA interception, ADB-based device control, and AI-assisted victim targeting. A separate Android RAT, ArcticRAT, similarly uses LLMs and black-screen overlays to steal financial data and remotely control infected devices.

  • ThreatFabric identified Bazuka as a modular Android malware framework with a downloader, core component, and 23 modules for overlays, keylogging, SMS and two-factor-code interception, remote control, and cryptocurrency address replacement.
  • Bazuka can take a screenshot of a victim’s home or lock screen and display it as an overlay to conceal malicious activity occurring in the background.
  • Bazuka’s control panel includes large language model integration that operators can use to identify and score victims, and it supports both locally hosted models and API-accessed models.
  • Zimperium reported that ArcticRAT is an Android remote-access trojan that uses large language model APIs to analyze stolen SMS messages and app data for high-value financial information while using black-screen overlays to hide remote actions.

Technologies: mobile-os, remote-access

Products: android, google-play, google-play-protect, android-debug-bridge

Vendors: google, threatfabric, zimperium

Fake GTA VI PC client spreads malware through a ClickFix attack — Should Read

A fake GTA VI PC streaming client uses a ClickFix lure to trick Windows users into running PowerShell, ultimately installing a Rust-based information stealer. The malware can steal browser, gaming, cryptocurrency, and developer credentials while hiding through DLL side-loading and process injection.

  • A fake GTA VI PC streaming-client website instructs Windows users to press Win+R and run a PowerShell command that downloads and starts GTA6Cloud.exe.
  • GTA6Cloud.exe displays a GTA VI-themed decoy while downloading loadperf.dll and unlodctr.exe into a hidden folder under the user’s local AppData directory.
  • The attackers use the legitimate Windows program unlodctr.exe to load a malicious loadperf.dll, which injects an embedded Rust-based stealer into legitimate Windows processes.
  • The stealer can collect browser credentials, cookies, tokens, Discord and Steam data, cryptocurrency wallet data, AI and developer-service credentials, clipboard contents, and screenshots.
  • People who ran the command should treat the computer as compromised, disconnect it from the internet, scan it with trusted security software, and change important passwords from a separate clean device.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus, browser

Products: bitdefender-total-security, windows, powershell, gta-vi, tauri

Vendors: bitdefender, microsoft, rockstar-games, take-two-interactive, tauri

NSA resumes normal operations following internal network disruptions — Should Read

The NSA has largely restored normal operations after PHP-related maintenance disrupted its classified internal NSANet communications network for three days. Officials said the outage was not a cyberattack and did not impair key intelligence operations or support for the president’s Asia trip.

  • The National Security Agency mostly returned to normal operations after three days of disruptions to NSANet, its internal system for communicating classified information.
  • Officials attributed the disruptions to maintenance involving PHP patches that caused some systems not to restart as expected.
  • Some NSA facilities remained under Code Orange for non-essential employees, with delayed openings and requirements for some staff to check in with supervisors.
  • Workplace interruptions occurred at NSA Georgia, but sources said its Middle East-focused intelligence operations were not negatively affected.
  • Administration officials said the NSA problems were not caused by a cyberattack and were unrelated to recent IT issues affecting Microsoft products, airline travel, and online banking services.

Products: php, nsanet

Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind. — Optional

Sponsored by NordPass, the article argues that spreadsheets cannot reliably track changing and shared company credentials, creating security blind spots. It promotes using a managed business password vault to centralize storage, enforce stronger passwords, monitor sharing, and identify weak or exposed credentials.

  • Manually maintained password spreadsheets do not reliably capture credentials that employees create, change, store in browsers, or share through chat and other unofficial channels.
  • The article says employees often use unofficial password storage or sharing methods when the approved process is slow or unclear, making complete manual reporting difficult to sustain.
  • Verizon’s 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report found that, in the median case, only 49% of users’ passwords across services were unique.
  • The article states that ransomware groups such as Pysa have used scripts to search drives for files and folders with names such as “password,” “login,” “pwd,” and “passwd.”
  • The article promotes NordPass Business as a centralized password vault with tools to identify weak, reused, old, and exposed passwords and to review access to shared credentials.

Technologies: secrets-manager

Products: nordpass, data-breach-scanner, password-health, sharing-hub

Vendors: nordpass, verizon
